title: Grateful Dead Live at War Memorial on 1973-03-31
source: SBD > MC > CASS > DAT > CDA > DAW(Bertha) > Audio DVD > DVD Audio Extractor v.3.3.2 (audio files extracted prior to burning to DVD disc) > 24/48 wav > downsampled to 44.1 wav with Wave Lab v.5.00a > dithered to from 24-16 bit depth with Wave Lab UV22 HR Plugin > SBEs fixed with shntool v.2.0.3 (by set) > files rennamed with File Renamer v.1.0.0 > FLAC encoding with FLAC Frontend v.1.7.1 Etree Edition, FLAC v.1.1.2

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp mix and a high‑energy second set highlighted by He's Gone, Truckin', The Other One and Rider.
ai_review.review: The recording, sourced from the original 2nd‑gen cassette but cleaned up masterfully, delivers clear, well‑balanced audio despite a faint tape hiss. Musically the show shines – Jerry’s soaring guitar work and vocal conviction drive a standout second set that rolls through a rare He’s Gone > Truckin' > The Other One > Rider sequence, while Bertha, Greatest Story Ever Told and Box of Rain add extra sparkle.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers award 4‑5 stars, praising both performance and sound; only a few minor critiques keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced mix with occasional tape hiss; cleanup work praised for eliminating noise and delivering crisp instrument separation.

poor_songs: Other One (jam) – not as raging as expected
show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid first set followed by an unusually adventurous second set that strings together a rare He’s Gone > Truckin' > The Other One > Rider sequence, keeping the energy high and delivering memorable transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Frenzied, Roy‑Buchanan‑like guitar tone with soaring harmonics; strong vocal delivery on TLEO.
band_member_comments.Phil: Not a climactic vocal on Box of Rain but delivers an impressive run alongside Donna Jean.
band_member_comments.Drums: Early ’73 drumming noted for heavy snare and tom‑tom presence, adding drive to the set.
